events.note:
In Bondarewka-Hubon, at the entrance to the village in the forest, our reburial service exhumed 243 German soldiers from graves that were no longer visible above ground and had been partially plundered, and transported them to the war cemetery in Kyiv (Russian: Kiev). Not all of the dead reported for the location could be recovered.

Unfortunately, Hermann Zelmer's dog tag was not found on any of the recovered bodies. His identification was also not possible based on other clues. However, he is probably one of the German soldiers who rest in Block 5 of the German war cemetery in Kyiv .

The names are labelled successively according to the status of the reburials and identifications. The names of the war dead are listed in alphabetical order on granite steles, which are assigned to the respective grave blocks. Hermann Zelmer's personal details are already included there.

-Information from Anna Atropov, German War Graves Commission, 2025-01-13

notes: Refer to EWZ photos 930,932,936,938,242 and244.  Hermann Zelmer is known as person # 152769 in the EWZ registry and his father is EWZ # 28489being Wilhelm Zelmer. On photo #242 he is shown to be 172 cm or 5' -6.4" tall and weighs 61 kg or 134.5 lbs.  This data is in 1940 when Hermann was 19 years of age.  This same document refers to him as slender and wearing glasses. Living in transit. Julie, nee Tepper, born 1891 in Gross Gluscha, evang, living in transit.  Moved to Pabianice from Podborodsche, Kamien-Koszerski on Feb.2,1940. #0932-1:Only a portion of this document is transcribed here:Handwritten comments:Volksdeutscher, speaks fluently German, also Polish and Ukrainian.
